subject: DPA clarifications — controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@orionanalytics.com>, Ryan Moore <ryan.moore@orionanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA clarifications — follow-up from today's call

Hi Samantha / Ryan,

Thanks for the time this morning — great to learn more about Orion's ingestion volumes and retention needs. Per our discussion, I'm following up with the specific DPA/privacy items you asked us to clarify so you can share with your legal/compliance team. Attached is our current DPA for reference (Redwood_DPA_v1.2.pdf).

Key items you raised:
1) Controller vs Processor: Please confirm you view Orion as the Controller and Redwood as the Processor for customer-provided data. We are happy to reflect that in the DPA; I want to make sure we use the same language.
2) Subprocessors: You asked for a full list of subprocessors (cloud infra, monitoring, email, analytics) and the notice/objection process for adding new subprocessors.
3) Breach notice & timeline: You mentioned a preference for a 48-hour initial notification for customer-impacting incidents; our standard commitment is 72 hours once an incident is confirmed.
4) Data residency & deletion: Confirmation on regional routing (US/EU) and certificate of deletion within a specific window on termination.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the controller/processor expectation above?
- I'll loop in legal (cc'd) to draft proposed language for subprocessors, timeline, and deletion certification.
- If useful, please send your compliance questionnaire and any specific contract language you prefer.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate next steps once I hear back from you and Legal.

Best,
Ben
---

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@orionanalytics.com>

Hi Ben,

Thanks for summarizing. Quick responses from our side:

- Controller/Processor: Yes, Orion is the Controller for customer data; we expect Redwood to operate as Processor. Please confirm you will accept Processor-only obligations in the DPA.

- Subprocessors: We need a current list of subprocessors and a commitment to provide at least 30 days' notice before onboarding any new subprocessor that will process customer data. We also expect an objection right if the new subprocessor's role or location raises regulatory concerns (e.g., cross-border transfers to non-approved jurisdictions). Please confirm whether Redwood's infrastructure partners (e.g., cloud providers) are included.

- Breach notification: Our legal team generally requests initial notification within 48 hours of discovery for incidents that materially impact customer data, with follow-up updates. Is Redwood willing to commit to 48 hours? If not, please explain the practical constraints.

- Data residency & deletion: We are evaluating EU residency for a subset of customers. Please confirm whether you can (1) guarantee EU regional routing and (2) provide a certificate of deletion within 30 days after contract termination for hosted deployments.

I've attached our compliance questionnaire (not included here). Once we have Redwood's responses and the current subprocessor list we'll share with our GC.

Thanks,
Samantha Li
Head of Security & Compliance
Orion Analytics

Subject: RE: DPA clarifications — controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice

Ben / Dev,

Thanks for the ping — below is proposed guidance and contract language snippets we can share with Orion. Happy to jump on a quick call with their GC if helpful.

Summary positions (recommended):
- Controller/Processor: Redwood acknowledges Orion as Controller and Redwood as Processor. We will accept Processor obligations in the DPA (data processing only; Controller retains direction of personal data).

- Subprocessors: We maintain an up-to-date subprocessor roster and will provide it to customers on request. Current categories include:
  * Cloud infrastructure providers (AWS, GCP)
  * Monitoring / telemetry (Datadog)
  * Email / notifications (SendGrid)
  * Logging & analytics (Snowflake for aggregated telemetry)
  * Deployment & orchestration partners (third-party managed services)

  Proposed commitments to offer Orion:
  * Provide the current subprocessor list in CSV (attached: subprocessor_list_2027-04-16.csv).
  * Provide at least 30 days' notice before engaging a new subprocessor that will process customer data.
  * Offer a reasonable objection process: if Orion objects in writing within the notice period based on legitimate regulatory concerns, Redwood and Orion will meet to discuss mitigation or alternatives (e.g., restricted routing, contractual controls, or Private deployment).

- Breach notification: Our standard practice is to notify affected customers without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that materially affects customer data. Operationally, 72 hours allows time to verify facts and scope before notification.
  * We can commit to immediate internal escalation and an initial customer status update as soon as materially confirmed.
  * If Orion requires a firm 48-hour SLA for initial notification for certain incident types, we can discuss a targeted amendment limited to incidents meeting a defined "material impact" threshold, subject to operational feasibility and mutual agreement.

- Data residency & deletion:
  * Hosted: We support regional routing and can commit to routing EU customer workloads to EU regions where available; however, hosted routing is subject to capacity and model availability.
  * Private deployments: For strict residency requirements, offer Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment with explicit region control.
  * Deletion: We will delete customer data as specified in the DPA and can provide a certificate of deletion within 30 days following verified deletion for hosted accounts.

Suggested DPA language snippets (for Orion legal):
- "Controller and Processor. Customer (Orion Analytics) is the Controller of customer data and Redwood Inference is the Processor. Redwood will process personal data only on documented instructions from Customer and in accordance with the DPA."
- "Subprocessors. Redwood maintains a list of subprocessors. Redwood will provide Customer with prior notice of any new subprocessor and will provide at least thirty (30) days for Customer to object on reasonable grounds related to data protection law. If Customer objects, the Parties will engage in good faith discussions to address Customer's concerns."
- "Breach Notification. Redwood will notify Customer without undue delay and, where feasible, within seventy-two (72) hours of confirming a security incident that materially affects Customer data. Notification will include available details, steps taken, and remediation plans, and will be followed by regular updates as information becomes available."
- "Data Residency & Deletion. Redwood will, where available, route Customer data to Customer-specified regions and will provide evidence of deletion upon request within thirty (30) days of verified deletion for hosted customers. For strict residency requirements, Customer may elect a Private deployment."

Attachments: subprocessor_list_2027-04-16.csv (current roster).

Next steps:
- Ben: send the above summary + subprocessor CSV to Orion and ask if they want the 48-hour carveout to be limited to incidents meeting a specific materiality definition.
- If they push back on notice/objection mechanics, propose a short call between our GC and their GC.

Happy to revise the language if Orion's legal sends redlines.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
